title: In re James Whisler, Case No. 25-180C (Lyon County School District Trustee)
text:
STATE OF NEVADA
BEFORE THE NEVADA COMMISSION ON ETHICS
In re James Whisler, Trustee, Ethics Complaint
Lyon County School District,
Case No. 25-180C
Lyon County, State of Nevada,
Subject. /
DEFERRAL AGREEMENT
NRS 281A.740
1. On January 21, 2026, a Review Panel authorized the Executive Director of
the Nevada Commission on Ethics (“Commission”) and James Whisler (“Whisler”) to
develop this Deferral Agreement (the “Agreement”) to address the alleged conduct at
issue in Ethics Complaint No. 25-180C (“Complaint”) instead of referring the Complaint
to the Commission for further proceedings.
2. At all material times, Whisler is a public officer as defined in NRS 281A.160.
The Ethics in Government Law (“Ethics Law”) set forth in NRS Chapter 281A gives the
Commission jurisdiction over Whisler as a public officer whose conduct is alleged to have
violated the provisions of NRS Chapter 281A. See NRS 281A.280.
3. This Agreement is entered into based upon the January 21, 2026 Review
Panel Determination that Whisler’s alleged conduct may be appropriately addressed
through the terms and conditions of a deferral agreement instead of referring the
Complaint to the Commission for further proceedings.
4. The Review Panel Determination was based on facts established by
sufficient evidence to support just and sufficient cause for the Commission to render an
opinion in the matter. The facts relied upon by the Review Panel to make its determination
are summarized in Appendix A (“Relevant Facts Relied Upon by the Review Panel”).1
1 The Relevant Facts Relied Upon by the Review Panel do not constitute part of the “Investigative File” as
that term is defined by NRS 281A.755. All statutory and common law protections afforded to the
Investigative File shall remain and are not affected by this Agreement.

5. No findings have been made by the Review Panel or the Commission that
Whisler violated the Ethics Law, and this Agreement does not constitute an admission by
Whisler of any violation of the Ethics Law.
A. Procedural History:
1. On September 26, 2025, the Commission received Ethics Complaint No.
25-180C regarding Whisler, alleging violations of Ethics Law provisions NRS 281A.400(1)
and (2) and NRS 281A.420(1) and (3).
2. On November 13, 2025, Whisler was sent a Notice of Complaint,
Investigation, and Notice of Additional Issues and Facts to inform him the allegations
regarding NRS 281A.400(1) and (2) were dismissed and that the allegations regarding
NRS 281A.420(1) and (3) were accepted by the Commission for investigation.
3. On November 13, 2025, the Commission issued an Order on Jurisdiction
and Investigation directing the Executive Director to conduct an investigation regarding
Whisler’s alleged violations of the following provisions of the Ethics Law:
NRS 281A.420(1) Failing to sufficiently disclose the acceptance of
a gift or loan, pecuniary interest, commitment in a private capacity to
the interest of another person or the nature of any representation or
counseling provided to a private person for compensation before
another agency in the preceding year that is reasonably affected by
an official matter.
NRS 281A.420(3) Failing to abstain from acting on an official
matter which is materially affected by the acceptance of a gift or loan,
pecuniary interest, or commitment in a private capacity to the interest
of another person.
4. The Notice of Complaint, Investigation, and Notice of Additional Issues and
Facts provided Whisler a deadline of December 17, 2025 for submitting a response to the
allegations.
5. On November 18, 2025 Whisler provided a timely written response to the
allegations.
6. On January 12, 2026, the Executive Director presented a recommendation
relating to just and sufficient cause to a three-member review panel pursuant to NRS
281A.725.
7. A Review Panel Determination was issued on January 21, 2026 concluded
the following:
Deferral Agreement
Case No. 25-180C

The Review Panel unanimously finds and concludes that the facts do
establish credible evidence to support a determination that just and
sufficient cause exists for the Commission to render an opinion in the
matter regarding the alleged violation of NRS 281A.420(1) and (3).
Pursuant to NRS 281A.730, the Review Panel reasonably believes that
Subject’s conduct may be appropriately addressed through corrective
action under the terms and conditions of a deferral agreement instead
of referring these allegations to the Commission for further proceedings.
B. Terms and Conditions of Deferral Agreement:
1. This Agreement shall be in effect for a period of one (1) year (the “Deferral
Period”) from the date of the executed Deferral Agreement.
2. Whisler must comply in all material respects with the Ethics Law during the
Deferral Period and must not become the subject of another ethics complaint arising from
conduct occurring during the Deferral Period for which a Review Panel determines just
and sufficient cause exists for the Commission to determine that he violated the Ethics
Law.
3. Whisler must schedule and attend ethics training approved by the
Commission within 60 days from the date of the executed Deferral Agreement, specifically
addressing the disclosure and abstention requirements of NRS 281A.420.
4. Whisler agrees to certify that he has read and understands the requirements
of NRS 281A.420 and the Commission’s Ethics Manual chapter on Disclosure and
Abstention within 30 days of approval of this agreement.
5. Whisler will submit Lyon County School District Board of Trustees meeting
minutes reflecting any appropriate disclosures and abstentions during Board meetings to
the Executive Director for 6 months following the approval of this agreement.
6. During the Deferral Period, the Executive Director shall monitor Whisler’s
compliance with this Agreement. Should the Executive Director discover that Whisler has
not complied with any term or condition of this Agreement, the Executive Director shall:
a. Inform the Commission of any alleged failure of Whisler to comply with
this Agreement;
b. Give Whisler written notice of any alleged failure to comply with this
Agreement; and
c. Allow Whisler not less than 15 days to respond to such a notice.

7. The Commission may vacate this Agreement and conduct further
proceedings in the matter, including an adjudicatory hearing, if the Commission finds that
Whisler failed to comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
8. If Whisler complies with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the
Commission shall dismiss this complaint with prejudice.
9. This Agreement applies only to the alleged conduct related to this
Complaint.
C. Acceptance: We, the undersigned parties, have read this Agreement, understand
each and every provision therein, and agree to be bound thereby.

Appendix A
1. Whisler currently serves as an elected Trustee for the Lyon County School
District Board of Trustees.
2. Whisler is married to a Lyon County School District teacher, and his mother-
in-law is employed as a certified teacher for the District.
3. On September 23, 2025, the Board of Trustees considered approval of the
collective bargaining agreement between the District and the LCEA as part of
the Consent Agenda Item 10.D.
4. The proposed agreement included: a 2% wage increase over two years for
employees of the District; pay increases for time spent on Individual
Education Plans, Student Study Teams, Section 504 Plans and other various
changes to the working conditions at the District.
5. The consent agenda was introduced, Trustee Farr moved to approve it and
Whisler seconded the motion.
6. The consent agenda, including Item 10.D, passed unanimously with Whisler
voting in favor.
7. At no time during the September 23, 2025 meeting did Whisler disclose his
spouse’s and mother-in-law’s employment with the District or abstain from
voting on a matter affecting their compensation and employment benefits.
8. Whisler’s spouse and mother-in-law received not greater or lesser benefit
from the agreement approved in Consent Agenda Item 10.D than others in
the collective bargaining unit.
9. Whisler sought legal guidance from the legal counsel for the Lyon County
School District Board of Trustees who failed to provide accurate guidance
regarding disclosure and abstention requirements in the Ethics Law.
